cards.text: Back in 1 Chronicles 17:10, God made David a promise: "And I will subdue all your enemies." Now it's some time later, and David heads out to war. Friend, tie that apron tight, because this chapter moves FAST.

cards.question: Some time after God's promise, David starts with an old enemy of Israel. Which people does David defeat and subdue first?

cards.text: David even takes Gath and its villages right out of the Philistines' hand. That's Goliath's hometown (1 Samuel 17:4), and I bet David didn't need anybody to give him directions.

cards.question: Next, David defeats the Moabites. What happens to Moab after that?

answers.text: They serve David and bring tribute
They flee and leave their land
They join David as equal partners

cards.text: Then the big one: Hadadezer, king of Zobah, marching out to establish his dominion along the Euphrates River. David defeats him as far as Hamath.

cards.question: David captures a thousand of King Hadadezer's chariots, plus thousands of his soldiers. What does David do with the horses?

cards.text: Then the Arameans of Damascus come to help Hadadezer, and David strikes down twenty-two thousand of their men. That's like running in to back up your friend in an argument, and now YOU'RE losing the argument too.

cards.question: David places garrisons in Aram of Damascus. True or false: the Arameans become subject to David and bring him tribute.
After all these wins, the chapter tells us who is behind them: So the ___ made David victorious wherever he went.

cards.text: David takes the gold shields that belonged to Hadadezer's officers and brings them to Jerusalem. I can't keep ONE white apron clean, and these officers had shields made of GOLD.

cards.question: From Tibhath and Cun, cities of King Hadadezer, David takes a large amount of bronze. Who later uses that bronze to make the bronze Sea and the pillars?
King Tou of Hamath hears that David defeated Hadadezer, who had been at war with Tou. So Tou sends his ___ Hadoram to greet King David and bless him.

cards.text: Hadoram brings all kinds of articles of gold and silver and bronze. Friend, that's not a thank-you card, that's a thank-you WAREHOUSE.

cards.question: King David now has Hadoram's gold, silver and bronze, plus the silver and gold he carried off from Edom, Moab, the Ammonites, the Philistines and the Amalekites. What does David do with all of it?

answers.text: Pays the men in his army

cards.text: And there's more. Abishai, son of David's sister Zeruiah (1 Chronicles 2:16), strikes down eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt.

cards.question: After the Valley of Salt, David places garrisons in Edom. True or false: only some of the Edomites become subject to David.
That line again: the LORD made David victorious wherever he went. Now David reigns over all Israel and administers ___ and ___ for all his people.

cards.text: David's got a whole crew, from Joab son of Zeruiah over the army to Zadok and Ahimelech as priests, and David's sons are chief officials at the king's side. My crew? Me, my mustache and one very patient oven.

findings.problem: The question says David 'starts with' the Philistines and asks which people he defeats 'first.' 1 Chronicles 18:1-2 lists the victories and joins them with 'also,' but it never says the Philistine campaign came first. Card 4's 'Next, David defeats the Moabites' adds the same order.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The joke 'I bet David didn't need anybody to give him directions' only works if the baker knows David went to Gath before (1 Samuel 21, 27). No card sets that up. Being Goliath's hometown doesn't mean David knew the way there, so a stranger would say 'huh?'

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.

findings.problem: The fact is David taking the gold shields and bringing them to Jerusalem. The joke compares something else: Papa Dorin failing to keep an apron clean versus officers owning gold shields. The comparison doesn't share the card's core action, so the punchline doesn't land cleanly.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess Hadoram's relationship to Tou (son, brother or servant). Nothing on the earlier cards lets them reason it out. It tests a detail they haven't seen, not meaning they can work out.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The card says 'David places garrisons in Edom.' But 1 Chronicles 18:13 says 'He placed garrisons in Edom' right after 18:12 names Abishai, so the text leaves open who placed them. The card settles it as David.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The story card runs to three sentences ('David's got a whole crew... at the king's side.' / 'My crew?' / 'Me, my mustache and one very patient oven.'). Only the opening card may go past two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
